sources.fact: Historic authoritative Brownfield record LBBD45 identifies 58 to 62 Church Street.
That Brownfield record ended on 20 February 2025 and is treated as historical rather than current status.
The historical register maximum was 6 net dwellings; it is not treated as a current adopted capacity.
The historical register status was not-permissioned.
The historical Brownfield ownership category says owned-by-a-public-authority; category is not a named proprietor/title.

The older Site Specific Allocations DPD identifies Policy SSA SM27, 58-62 Church Street, and records private ownership with potential wider development incorporating council-owned 64-68 Church Street.
Older DPD private-ownership wording versus later Brownfield public-authority category is preserved as time/scope conflict and not silently reconciled.
Regulation 19 Cabinet HTML lists S_ZT - 58 to 62 Church Street as a site-allocation attachment, verifying allocation identity without importing PDF detail.
18/01215/FUL at land rear of 20-30 Church Street was refused under delegated powers on 9 October 2018.
The Planning Inspectorate appeal for the separate 20-30 Church Street case was dismissed on 1 March 2019.
The separate 20-30 Church Street refusal/appeal is not transferred to ZT 58-62 Church Street solely because of street-name proximity.

examples.result: LBBD45 is historical and ended in February 2025.
Historical 6-home maximum is not asserted as current ZT capacity.
Historical not-permissioned status is not silently projected into 2026.
Public-authority category is not a named HMLR owner.
Older private-ownership wording and later category conflict is preserved rather than overwritten.
20-30 Church Street case 18/01215/FUL is a separate site and is not bound to ZT.
Regulation 19 HTML verifies allocation identity but inaccessible attachment details are not imported.
Promotion remains zero until current exact case, title topology and overlays are verified.
